about: Places of interest stage 5: the famous places' own facts the map doesn't hold. Each finds its place by the word in its name (match) within km of at; kind, radius (m), tall (m), stones, banks, spire, banded, lintels, fallen, unlit say how it's drawn; note is what the sat nav says on arriving; add puts it in where the map hasn't got it.

sites.name: Castlerigg Stone Circle
sites.note: 38 stones, about 5,000 years old

sites.name: Swinside Stone Circle
sites.note: 55 stones, also called Sunkenkirk

sites.name: Long Meg and Her Daughters
sites.note: 59 stones, one of the largest circles in England

sites.name: Stonehenge
sites.note: Built about 2500 BC, lines up with the midsummer sunrise

sites.name: Avebury
sites.note: The largest stone circle in Britain, a village inside it

sites.name: Ring of Brodgar
sites.note: 27 of its 60 stones still standing

sites.name: Calanais Standing Stones
sites.note: 13 stones round a tall middle stone, about 5,000 years old

sites.name: Rollright Stones
sites.note: The King's Men, about 70 weathered stones

sites.name: Arbor Low
sites.note: Every stone lying down, inside a great bank

sites.name: Merry Maidens
sites.note: 19 stones, said to be girls turned to stone for dancing on a Sunday

sites.name: Rudston Monolith
sites.note: The tallest standing stone in Britain, 7.6 m

sites.name: Devil's Arrows
sites.note: Three great stones in a line, the tallest 6.9 m

sites.name: Flamborough Head Lighthouse
sites.note: Built in 1806, 26.5 m

sites.name: Beachy Head Lighthouse
sites.note: Stands in the sea under the cliffs, 1902

sites.name: Souter Lighthouse
sites.note: The first lighthouse built for electric light, 1871

sites.name: St Bees Lighthouse
sites.note: On the cliffs at the start of the Coast to Coast walk

sites.name: Portland Bill Lighthouse
sites.note: 41 m, lit since 1906

sites.name: Hoad Monument
sites.note: A lighthouse with no light, for Sir John Barrow, 1850

sites.name: Stoodley Pike
sites.note: 37 m, built in 1856 for the peace after the Crimean War

sites.name: Captain Cook's Monument
sites.note: On Easby Moor, where Cook grew up, 1827

sites.name: Wainhouse Tower
sites.note: 84 m, the tallest folly in the world, 1875

sites.name: Hardy Monument
sites.note: For Nelson's flag captain at Trafalgar, 1844

sites.name: Maiden Castle
sites.note: One of the largest Iron Age hillforts in Europe

sites.name: British Camp
sites.note: On the Herefordshire Beacon, Iron Age ramparts
